method.method_draft: Set variables from the picture: let H be the table height, B the bottle height, and C the can height. Read the first configuration as a vertical distance from the top of the floor can to the top of the tabletop bottle, so H + B - C = 150. Read the second configuration as a vertical distance from the top of the floor bottle to the top of the tabletop can, so H + C - B = 110. Add the two equations to cancel B and C: 2H = 260, hence H = 130 cm.

method.method_draft: Interpret the two measurements as symmetric deviations from the table height. When the bottle is on the table and the can is on the floor, the measured distance equals the table height plus the bottle-can height difference. When the can is on the table and the bottle is on the floor, the measured distance equals the table height minus that same bottle-can height difference. Therefore the table height is the average of the two measured distances: (150 + 110) / 2 = 130 cm.
